title: DECISION: DID verify is non-blocking (articles accepted on failure)
description: When the X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header is present but verification fails (parse error, bad encoding, or invalid signature), the article is still accepted and stored. The result is recorded as Option<bool> in the overview index: Some(true) = verified, Some(false) = sig present but invalid, None = header absent or unparseable. This is correct because DID signing is an optional author-asserted layer on top of mandatory operator signing. Rejecting articles on DID verify failure would let any peer craft a malformed DID-Sig header to drop another user's articles — a denial-of-service vector. The verification outcome is preserved for clients that want to filter or display it.
